breaking.headline: Anthropic to price its IPO Wednesday; demand reportedly 6x oversubscribed
breaking.fact: Anthropic is set to price its IPO Wednesday, Nov. 18, and begin trading Thursday on Nasdaq as ANT at $70 to $78 a share for 825 million shares, with demand reportedly about six times the shares on offer. Morningstar put fair value at $92 a share; a concurrent $26 billion private placement goes to strategic partners including Google, Nvidia and Microsoft.

breaking.headline: Trump leaves for Asia; first-ever Trump–Xi–Putin summit set for Thursday
breaking.fact: President Trump departs Washington Monday for Manila, where he attends the ASEAN summit and plans to sign a trade deal with Thailand, then flies to Shenzhen for APEC. On Thursday he holds a bilateral with Xi Jinping, then the first-ever three-way meeting of the U.S., Chinese and Russian leaders, focused on nuclear arms and the Iran war — Ukraine is not on the agenda and no deal is expected.

breaking.headline: Estonia to shut all Russia border crossings Dec. 1 after GRU-blamed arson plot
breaking.fact: Estonia will close its three border crossings with Russia — Narva, Luhamaa and Koidula — from Dec. 1, Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna announced Sunday, after eight people were detained over an attempted arson attack on drone maker Threod Systems that Estonia’s security service blames on Russia’s GRU. The Kremlin called the claims “entirely baseless” Monday; no end date for the closure was given.

breaking.headline: Chip rout spreads: Taiwan down 6%, Nasdaq futures off 1.5% ahead of Nvidia earnings
breaking.fact: Taiwan’s Taiex fell 6.03% Monday and TSMC 5.74% as investors cut AI exposure ahead of Nvidia’s results Tuesday. Nasdaq 100 futures were down about 1.5% and S&P 500 futures about 0.7% early Monday, with Nvidia itself down roughly 4% pre-market to about $157 after falling 12% last week.

weekInBrief.headline: COP31 draft urges fossil-fuel phase-out as talks enter final week
weekInBrief.body: The Australian presidency circulated a draft decision Monday urging countries to speed up a fair phase-out of coal, oil and gas, remove fossil-fuel subsidies as soon as possible, and hold warming to 1.5°C, with adaptation finance to triple by 2035. But ministers arriving in Antalya for the final week remain split over the cover text, climate finance and Europe’s carbon border levy, and officials say the outcome will likely be decided at the last minute.

weekInBrief.headline: Hundreds of thousands rally in Prague against media-funding overhaul
weekInBrief.body: Organizers put Sunday’s turnout at about 400,000 in Prague — possibly the largest demonstration since the 1989 Velvet Revolution — against Prime Minister Babis’s plan to scrap the household broadcasting fee and fund public media from the state budget, which critics say would dent the broadcasters’ independence. The bill has passed a preliminary vote and awaits further debate.

weekInBrief.headline: Philippines and Australia sign defence pact with eye on China
weekInBrief.body: The Philippines and Australia signed a defence cooperation arrangement Sunday in Manila, updating a 1995 pact to cut bureaucratic hurdles to joint military activities under their visiting-forces deal. Manila said it bolsters its “credible deterrence posture” in the South China Sea; the signing came ahead of the ASEAN summit, which President Trump attends Tuesday.

weekInBrief.headline: Japan-led probe finds 1,000 servers behind AI-driven cyberattacks
weekInBrief.body: An international investigation led by Japan’s JPCERT/CC has identified about 1,000 servers online since October that hosted AI tools used to scan websites worldwide for vulnerabilities, findings released Nov. 14 showed. Investigators are still tracking 600 to 700 of the servers; one carried traces of a programming tool from Anthropic. The count is suspected attack infrastructure, not confirmed breaches.

items.headline: Latest from the Strait
items.body: The confrontation escalated again overnight: Iran’s navy said Monday a tanker caught fire after striking a mine east of the strait — the sixth tanker Iran has claimed hit a mine in two days, none of the claims independently verified — while the U.S. launched fresh airstrikes Sunday night on Iranian missile launchers at Bandar Lengeh and Sirik after Iranian forces attacked the U.S. base in Bahrain. The aircraft carrier USS Theodore Roosevelt arrived Sunday, the third U.S. carrier in the region, joining two other strike groups and an amphibious ready group carrying some 9,000 to 10,000 troops, and Gulf stock markets dipped Monday as investors weighed the attacks. On oil, the blockade still holds — Iranian crude is not getting out in any meaningful volume, while Reuters reported Monday that shipments of non-Iranian Gulf oil through the strait have nearly returned to pre-war levels.

space.headline: Musk unveils a bigger Starship V4 after the historic catch
space.body: Late Sunday, Elon Musk said Starship V4 will be about 70 metres long — roughly 40% longer than V3 — with nine engines, three more Raptor-Vacuums, and more than 60% extra propellant, after Ship 42’s first-ever catch of an orbital upper stage on Saturday. SPCX rose nearly 1% overnight on the milestone, and ARK’s Cathie Wood called the catch the start of a “mind-blowing” beginning; the booster catch remains unproven after Booster 22’s abort.

space.headline: New tool maps unintended CRISPR edits cell by cell
space.body: Salk scientists have built Superb-seq, a method that reads out all of a CRISPR edit’s on- and off-target changes plus their effects on gene activity at single-cell resolution, published Monday in Nature Methods. In 10,000 human leukemia cells it detected 43 edit sites — 36 of them off-target — and 5,761 edited cells, giving researchers a far sharper picture of what a guide RNA actually does.

space.headline: Fossils reveal a 66-pound rodent from 34 million years ago
space.body: Two fossilized teeth from a coal mine in Thailand’s Krabi Province have named a new giant rodent, Yakamys sirindhornae, that lived about 34 million years ago and weighed roughly 30 kilograms (66 pounds) — far larger than other rodents of its time. The find, published Nov. 4 in Scientific Reports, suggests rodent gigantism began earlier and across a wider geography than previously thought.

space.headline: A single spark can ripple across an ultra-thin energy material
space.body: An international team including Victoria University of Wellington researchers found that a chemical reaction triggered at just one tiny point on an ultra-thin MXene flake can spread across much of the material — connectivity never seen before in this class of materials. Published in Nature Communications, the finding sheds new light on how water, electricity and hydrogen interact inside materials being explored for faster, more sustainable energy storage.

apod.title: NGC 7129: Star Formation with Jets from Webb
apod.credit: NASA, ESA, CSA, STScI, JWST; Processing: A. Pagan (STScI) — NASA Astronomy Picture of the Day, November 16, 2026
apod.explanation: NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope took this detailed infrared look at the star-forming region NGC 7129: young stars shine through gold-colored gas on the left, while jets and winds from newborn stars sculpt the red, filamentary gas on the right. Studying stars at different stages of development helps astronomers pin down which physical processes matter most, and when, in star formation.
